Not food, but was a delivery driver for a furniture rental store.

The fun deliveries are going to dilapidated, roach and spider infested trailers to set up a brand new 65" tv, only to soak in a hatred that only trailer-folk can provide as you explain that their expensive tv doesn't have a built-in antenna (because why would it?), and that, "Yes, you do need to get internet if you want to watch Netflix."

That wasn't a rare occurrence either. It was at least once or twice a week, sometimes more.

Food guys are lucky. You get to leave as quickly as you come. I had to wade through shit in these peoples' basements as I hooked up a washer and dryer set that I would ultimately be repossessing a month later.

The only thing that really bothers you after doing that job for awhile are the smells. You can always pick out the drunks because their house will smell like fresh vomit becasue they've thrown up so many times on their couches or carpets that they can't get the smel out. Animal smells are really common, because most of those people had no idea how to take care or clean up after a dog or cat.

But the worst that comes to mind was the house of an old senile woman. Her house smelled like she had stuffed her walls with rotten raw chicken. It was one of the most powerful bad smellls I've ever encountered, and I had to spend a little over a half hour in there.

I made barely over minimum wage.
